title: Understanding Trap Seal Integrity and Venting
description: A P-trap relies on a standing water barrier to block sewer gases from leaking into habitated spaces. However, when wastewater rushes down a drainage pipe, it creates a atmospheric pressure differential. Without proper venting, this negative pressure draws air through the trap, siphoning away the standing water seal. Professional plumbers prevent this by maintaining correct developed pipe lengths between the fixture trap and its vent connection. Checking for adequate airflow and protecting vents from blockages ensures that atmospheric pressure remains balanced, preserving the essential water seal in every fixture trap.

Understanding Trap Seal Integrity and Venting

A P-trap relies on a standing water barrier to block sewer gases from leaking into habitated spaces. However, when wastewater rushes down a drainage pipe, it creates a atmospheric pressure differential. Without proper venting, this negative pressure draws air through the trap, siphoning away the standing water seal. Professional plumbers prevent this by maintaining correct developed pipe lengths between the fixture trap and its vent connection. Checking for adequate airflow and protecting vents from blockages ensures that atmospheric pressure remains balanced, preserving the essential water seal in every fixture trap.
